newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: INTERVIEW-Mantex sees 50 pct export rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Mantex sees 50 pct export rise.

text.p: Venezuelan industrial conglomerate Mantex expects its exports to increase 50 percent to $45 million in 1997, company President Elias Zerbib told Reuters Wednesday.
"Exports for this year should be about $45 million and total sales about $70 million," Zerbib said in an interview.
A large part of the export growth was expected to come from Mantex's Acetco unit, which produces acetate for cigarette filters and textile filaments.
Acetco, which is 49 percent owned by Mantex and 51 percent by French group Rhone-Poulenc, will export $38 million in 1997 from total sales of between $55 and $60 million, Zerbib said.
Acetco's exports totaled $20 million in 1996, he said.
With strong growth in the acetate sector foreseen in coming years, Acetco's installed capacity will be raised to 15,000 tonnes annually during the next year, from 13,000 tonnes annually at present.
Capacity was raised by 40 percent in 1996 through a $3.7 million investment program.

Petpack, a polyester resin manufacturer in which Mantex also owns 49 percent, should see its margins improve towards the end of the year after strong price competition from Asian-produced products, Zerbib added.
The other 51 percent of Petpack, which should see exports of $7 million this year, is owned by Rodia Ster, a Brazilian subsidiary of Rhone-Poulenc.
In its textile products, Mantex took the decision earlier this year to concentrate on filaments and abandon fibers and threads, Zerbib said.
"There is greater stability in filaments, which go to small and medium industries. So since Jan 1 we decided to stop participating in the fibers business," he said.
That decision may affect Mantex's 50-50 partnership with fellow Venezuelan company Sudamtex in Polyquim, he added.
"We told Sudamtex there was no point in producing (fibers and threads) if there was no chance of success," Zerbib said.
Mantex reported net profits of 6.818 billion in 1996, up 39 percent in nominal terms from 1995. Net revenue per share was 9.06 bolivars against 7.15 bolivars in 1995.

Its main products are acetate, polyester resins and polyester filaments. It's main export markets are Brazil, Colombia, Chile, Central America, the Dominican Republic, Bolivia, China and South Africa.
